original_question: Give a purely combinatorial proof that every real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c_0 is oscillation stable, where oscillation stable means that for every epsilon > 0 there is an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that the oscillation of the map on the unit sphere of Y is at most epsilon, and do so without using ultrafilters.
target_in_paper: The draft most closely targets the unnumbered research direction stated immediately after Theorem 11 in Section 8 ("Bounded distortion"): obtain a purely combinatorial proof, avoiding ultrafilters, of Gowers’s theorem that every real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c_0 is oscillation stable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it names the right theorem-level content (Theorem 11), keeps the domain and codomain correct (a real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c_0), states the ε-subspace meaning of oscillation stability, and includes the paper’s extra desideratum that the proof be purely combinatorial and avoid ultrafilters. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
missing_details: The paper does not present this as a numbered conjecture or problem; the exact target is the sentence immediately following Theorem 11 in Section 8. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
To make the question stand alone, the domain should be written explicitly as S_{c_0}={x in c_0 : ||x||_∞=1}, with c_0 carrying its usual sup norm. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
The subspace Y should be identified as an infinite-dimensional linear subspace of c_0, and its sphere should be written as S_Y={y in Y : ||y||_∞=1}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

The oscillation condition should be stated explicitly as sup{|f(y)-f(z)| : y,z in S_Y} <= ε. The paper introduces oscillation stability exactly through this ε-small oscillation-on-a-subspace formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

To match the paper’s wording more faithfully, the proof method to be avoided is not only ultrafilters in the abstract but the known proofs via topological dynamics on βN. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

The nearby context in Section 8 first defines oscillation stability for real-valued Lipschitz maps on unit spheres of arbitrary infinite-dimensional Banach spaces; Theorem 11 is then the c_0-specific uniformly continuous instance. Keeping that distinction prevents accidental broadening. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
refined_question: Find a purely combinatorial proof, avoiding ultrafilters and the existing topological-dynamical arguments on βN, of Gowers’s theorem that for every uniformly continuous function f:S_{c_0}→R, where S_{c_0}={x∈c_0:||x||_∞=1}, and for every ε>0, there exists an infinite-dimensional linear subspace Y⊆c_0 such that sup{|f(y)-f(z)|:y,z∈S_Y}≤ε, where S_Y={y∈Y:||y||_∞=1}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
justification: Section 8 first recalls the notion of oscillation stability for real-valued Lipschitz maps on unit spheres, then states Theorem 11: every real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c_0 is oscillation stable. The very next sentence says that all known proofs of Theorem 11 use topological dynamics on βN and that it would be very interesting to have a purely combinatorial proof avoiding ultrafilters. So the draft is not really aiming at the numbered bounded-distortion problems (Problems 11 and 12), but at this specific post-Theorem-11 challenge, and the refined question above matches that target as narrowly as possible. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
